newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung shares slide ahead of court sentence.
newsitem.headline: Samsung shares slide ahead of court sentence.

text.p: Shares in the Samsung Group declined in mid-afternoon Monday trading ahead of the sentencing of the group's chairman on bribery charges, brokers said.

"The prospect of Lee Kun-hee's sentencing caused sentiment toward the group shares to decline," said a First Securities broker. "Because Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo both got severe sentences this morning as prosecutors had demanded, some jittery investors are expecting Lee to be sentenced to jail."
Prosecutors have asked for a prison sentence against Lee of three years on charges of giving 10 billion won in bribes.
Samsung Electronics fell 3,900 won to its limit- and year-low of 62,000. Samsung Fire Insurance fell 18,000 won to 403,000, while Samsung Display lost 1,800 won to 52,200.

But other brokers said the decline in Samsung shares were linked more to the plunge of Samsung Electronics. Samsung Electronics has been declining due to worries about further weakening in the global semiconductor market.

"The trial isn't having the biggest impact," said a Dongwon broker. "Most shares are falling today, and Samsung Electronics is leading the way for the group shares because of negative prospects on the memory chip front."
A Seoul District Court has already sentenced former president Chun Doo Hwan to death on charges related to a 1979 coup and an army massacre of pro-democracy demonstrators the following year.
His presidential successor, Roh Tae-woo, was sentenced to 22-1/2 years in prison on similar charges of masterminding the putsch that thrust Chun to power and of attempted murder of superior officers.
Both were found guilty of taking bribes. Chun was fined 225.9 billion won ($276 million) and Roh 283.8 billion won, equal to the amount they were convicted of pocketing.
